significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling: the claim's "canary signal drops with substantial lead time before behavioral safety ... breaks," and its drift velocity predicts when a fine-tuning trajectory will cross into behavioral collapse; it would additionally establish the form-(ii) result that a threshold-gated correction preserves safety with less utility loss than continuous constraints. The phenomenon is weighty because it fixes expectations about the temporal ordering of internal degradation and observable failure across future fine-tuning runs, while the mechanism is more limited: the harmfulness-recognition signal is a causal control point, but not a full circuit-level explanation of alignment erosion. The true and false states are determinate, and a negative result—lead time at or below zero or no advantage over random/static triggering—would rule out this specific internal signal and velocity-gating account, although it would not rule out other early-warning representations; this sharpens the benign-fine-tuning failure documented by Qi et al., "Fine-tuning Aligned Language Models Compromises Safety, Even When Users Do Not Intend To!" The topic-substitution check lowers no score: replacing the predictive temporal relation and conditional-control claim with the generic safety-interpretability topic would leave only a median direction-and-steering hypothesis, not this forecast law.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "canary drift features (value, velocity, curvature over a sliding window)" and the associated "drift-velocity-gated correction"; it is explicitly ex ante because it is intended to "halt or correct a run before it ships an unsafe model," giving operators an action window rather than merely explaining a completed failure. Although the harmfulness direction and threshold require per-model calibration, the substantive conclusion is a transferable predictive relation—re-extraction should recover internal drift preceding behavioral collapse by measurable lead time—rather than merely a procedure for searching for an unrelated direction anew. The hypothesis targets benign, outlier-benign, and poisoned fine-tuning across multiple model families and hands the result to fine-tuning-service operators who gate or ship models, though fixed-canary category coverage and adaptive suppression limit confidence that it travels to arbitrary safety failures. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: generic mechanistic safety work supplies neither an ex-ante per-step alarm nor a conditional deployment-control handle, so the reach comes from claim-specific lead time and operator uptake.
